_comment: Carry to R9-RO-9 (#1922) from R9-RO-5. The round-9 roster is not on main, so this file is the in-tree destination.
While this and the roster brief disagree, the newer is right.

carries.control: Run, at your merge base, a listing of git ls-files spelled through canon (counts.mjs canonList) and the same listing unspelled, and test the globs tools/audit/briefs/** and dev/governance/roles/** against each. On the R9-RO-5 head the old glob matched the canon spelling and none of the real paths, and the new glob matched the real paths and none of the canon spelling. The null is the other column: a glob that matches the real tree and not the canon list is what rule-binding reports as matching no tracked file, because that check reads the canon list. Re-run the same two columns. When they agree, this constraint is spent.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust the column result above. Re-run it at your merge base before editing a rule paths glob. policy-docs restores policy_lint.mjs and brief_lint.mjs from the base, and rule-binding walks the canon spelling.
carries.brief: R9-RO-9 drops the old-path lookup. In that same change, and not before, move each rule's paths globs off the canon spelling (tools/audit/briefs, docs/HANDOVER.md, docs/delivery, docs/plan) onto the paths the files have after R9-RO-5. A glob written only at the new path, while canon still spells listings the old way, is reported by rule-binding as matching no tracked file, on the restored grader as well as on the branch. Leaving the globs on the old spelling after canon is removed is the other failure: they then match nothing. The two edits are one edit.

carries.from: R9-RCA-1990 (#1990): R9-RO-6 and R9-RO-5 moved app_approve.sh, preflight.sh, app_comment.sh and the delivery rows, and five seat instruments kept the old paths
carries.control: tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py ran tools/audit/app_approve.sh after the move, so every carry printed `No such file or directory` and the train stopped, while its self-test, whose stub answers any argv containing a script's basename, stayed `43 checks, 0 failed`. Its self-test now reads the real tree: with TOOLS restored to the old paths alone and ROW_DIR to docs/delivery it prints `3 failed`, and with a bare `"bash", "tools/..."` argv it prints `1 failed` naming the path. The other seat scripts' self-tests stub their callees and do not see a missing path; bus.sh's poster pin is the exception (`grep -qxF` on its default line).
carries.remeasure: At your merge base, run `python3 tools/audit/seat/moved_paths.py tools/audit/seat/*` after your move: it lists every reference to a path tests/layout.json marks moved (each retired file absent from the tree, its emptied parent directory, each lifted prefix). Directories and documents count, not only scripts; a script-only grep missed `tools/audit/briefs/` in round 1 of #2012. A reference your move empties is re-pointed in the same commit, unless it is an old-path-first fallback naming the new path. Then run `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test`, `bash tools/audit/seat/bus.sh --self-test` and `python3 tools/audit/seat/handover_prompt.py --self-test` and show 0 failed.
carries.brief: A move re-points every seat instrument that invokes the moved path, in the move commit. merge_train.py resolves its scripts through its TOOLS table (old path first, then new) and ROW_DIR: a move edits those entries, and retiring an old lookup deletes only the old half of each tuple.
